paragraphs.title: The Righteous King and Peace in the Land

easy.explanation: The psalm asks God to give the king His judgments and righteousness.
easy.q: What does the king receive from God in verse 1?

easy.explanation: The king will judge God's people with righteousness and the poor with judgment.
easy.q: Whom will the king judge with righteousness?

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that the king shall break the oppressor in pieces.
easy.q: What will the king do to the oppressor?

medium.explanation: The mountains bring peace, and the little hills bring it by righteousness.
medium.q: What do the mountains and little hills bring to the people?

answers: Someone who mistreats or exploits others
medium.explanation: The oppressor is the person whom the righteous king defeats and restrains.
medium.q: In this passage, what is an oppressor?

answers: Saving the children of the needy
medium.explanation: The king saves the children of the needy and judges the poor fairly.
medium.q: Which action especially shows the king's care for the weak?

answers: Righteous judgment, protection of the weak, and peace
challenge.explanation: The passage presents righteous rule that protects the needy and produces peace.

answers: Because peace belongs only to kings
challenge.explanation: The passage presents peace as the result of righteous and fair rule.
challenge.q: Why is peace connected with righteousness in these verses?

answers: His only role is to punish
He combines justice with protection for the weak
He must remain distant from the people
challenge.explanation: The king is portrayed as one who administers justice and rescues the needy.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the king both judges and saves?

paragraphs.title: Reverence for God, Rain, and Enduring Peace

easy.explanation: The verse says they will fear God as long as the sun and moon endure, throughout all generations.
easy.q: How long will people fear God according to verse 5?

answers: Rain and showers watering the earth
easy.explanation: The king is compared to rain upon mown grass and showers that water the earth.
easy.q: What is the king's coming down compared to?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, 'In his days shall the righteous flourish.'
easy.q: Who shall flourish in the king's days?

medium.explanation: Rain watering the earth suggests refreshment, abundance, and blessing.
medium.q: What does the rain represent in this passage?

medium.explanation: The word refers to rain that waters and refreshes the earth.
medium.q: What are 'showers' in the context of verse 6?

answers: Fear of God, flourishing righteousness, and abundant peace
medium.explanation: These verses join reverence for God, the flourishing of the righteous, and abundant peace.
medium.q: Which combination describes the restored land?

answers: His rule brings blessing and refreshment
His rule brings danger to the land
challenge.explanation: Rain falling on the earth pictures a rule that nourishes and blesses the people.
challenge.q: What does the image of rain suggest about the king's rule?

answers: They are presented together as blessings of the king's days
The righteous flourish only during war
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 places the flourishing of the righteous alongside abundant peace.
challenge.q: How are the flourishing of the righteous and abundant peace related?

answers: Peace continues for a very long time
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the enduring and lasting nature of the peace.
challenge.q: What does 'so long as the moon endureth' emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The King's Power and the Submission of Nations

answers: From sea to sea and from the river to the ends of the earth
easy.explanation: Verse 8 describes the king's dominion as extending from sea to sea and to the ends of the earth.
easy.q: Over what area does the king have dominion?

easy.explanation: The verse says that his enemies shall lick the dust.
easy.q: What will the king's enemies do?

easy.explanation: The kings of Tarshish and the isles shall bring presents.
easy.q: What will the kings of Tarshish and the isles bring?

answers: Bow before him and serve him
medium.explanation: All kings shall fall down before him, and all nations shall serve him.
medium.q: What will all kings and all nations do before the king?

medium.explanation: The expression pictures the enemies as humbled and defeated.
medium.q: What does 'lick the dust' communicate in this passage?

answers: They bring presents and offer gifts
medium.explanation: The kings bring presents and offer gifts in addition to bowing before him.
medium.q: How is the submission of the nations shown besides bowing?

answers: The vast extent of the king's dominion
challenge.explanation: The phrase highlights the great breadth of the king's rule.
challenge.q: What does the phrase 'from sea to sea' emphasize?

answers: They recognize the king's honor and authority
They intend to end his rule
challenge.explanation: Gifts and homage show recognition of the king's status and worth.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the nations bringing gifts instead of merely submitting?

answers: The reach of his rule and the goodness of his influence
The wealth of his enemies alone
challenge.explanation: The passage combines the king's authority with the beneficial character of his reign.
challenge.q: Which combination best explains why the king receives honor?

paragraphs.title: Rescue of the Poor and Blessing of the Land

easy.explanation: The king delivers the needy when they cry and helps the poor who have no helper.
Verse 14 says he shall redeem their soul from deceit and violence.
easy.q: From what does he redeem their souls?

easy.explanation: The passage describes corn, fruit, and flourishing growth throughout the land.
easy.q: What happens to the land under this rule?

medium.explanation: The verse says, 'He shall spare the poor and needy.'
medium.q: How does the king treat the poor and needy?

answers: A small amount that produces abundant growth
A gift from a foreign king
medium.explanation: The image presents even a handful of corn as producing flourishing abundance.
medium.q: What does 'an handful of corn' represent in verse 16?

answers: Protective rule is accompanied by abundance and fruitfulness
Compassion prevents the land from growing
medium.explanation: The rescue of the weak is followed by pictures of a fruitful and blessed land.
medium.q: How are the king's compassion and the land's blessing connected?

answers: The person's helplessness and need for rescue
The person's opposition to the king
challenge.explanation: The phrase stresses that the poor person has no other source of help.
challenge.q: What does the phrase 'him that hath no helper' emphasize?

answers: Their lives have great value to him
He does not care about their suffering
challenge.explanation: Their precious blood shows that the king values and protects their lives.
challenge.q: What does it mean that the blood of the needy is precious in the king's sight?

answers: People and nations are blessed in him and call him blessed
His name disappears from the earth
challenge.explanation: Verse 17 says that men shall be blessed in him and all nations shall call him blessed.
challenge.q: How does the king's name become a symbol of blessing?

paragraphs.title: Blessing of the Lord and the Conclusion of David's Prayers

answers: The LORD God, the God of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 18 blesses the LORD God of Israel, who only does wondrous things.
The prayer asks that the whole earth be filled with the Lord's glory.
easy.q: What is requested to fill the whole earth?

easy.explanation: The final verse says, 'The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.'
easy.q: Whose prayers are ended in the final verse?

answers: A blessing of the Lord and a request that His glory fill the earth
A description of a final battle
medium.explanation: The ending blesses the Lord and asks for His glory to fill the whole earth.
medium.q: What is the structure of the psalm's ending?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the marvelous works performed by God.

answers: The lasting nature of the Lord's glorious name
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord's glorious name endures without end.
medium.q: What does 'for ever' emphasize in the blessing?

answers: It states that David's prayers have come to an end
It begins a new story about foreign kings
It cancels the blessing of the Lord
challenge.explanation: The final verse explicitly closes the prayers of David the son of Jesse.
challenge.q: How does the final verse relate to the conclusion of the psalm?

answers: Strong affirmation of the blessing and prayer
A rejection of what was said
challenge.explanation: The repeated 'Amen' strongly confirms the preceding blessing and request.
challenge.q: What does the repetition 'Amen, and Amen' communicate?

answers: The focus moves from blessed rule to praise of the Lord
The focus moves from peace to famine
The focus moves from the poor to warfare
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends by directing praise to God, the source of wondrous works and blessing.
challenge.q: What major shift occurs between the king's description and the psalm's ending?
